findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the following sanitizing operations were operating with too low sanitizer to be effective at sanitizing dishes:
(i) The triple sink was measured at 100 ppm (quaternary ammonium). CORRECTED: Staff determined that an extra pump of sanitizer shall be added to the triple sink to achieve 200ppm (3 pumps total). Inspector observed that the remade solution measured at an effective sanitizer level of 200ppm (quat). Ensure that the sanitizer concentration of quaternary ammonium is between 200-400ppm for safe and effective sanitizing for dishes.
(ii) The chemical dish machine was measured at less than 50ppm (Chlorine). CORRECTED: PIC were informed that the dish machine was too low for sanitizing and removed the dish machine from service immediately; staff instead would only do dishes in the triple sink instead of the supplementary chemical dish machine. Staff contacted a repair person, who arrived during the inspection and adjusted the dish machine. Inspector observes the repaired dish machine is sanitizing at 50ppm (Chlorine). Ensure that the sanitizer concentration of Chlorine is between 50-200ppm for safe and effective sanitizing for dishes.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed the cooler at the front service area (by the cash register) was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was about 50-60F, the internal thermometer was reading at 60F, and the opened jug of milk had an internal temperature of 55F. The PIC voluntary discarded all temperature control for safety (TCS) foods during the inspection: multiple jugs of milk, an opened container of oat milk, and orange juice. Non-TCS foods were kept inside the cooler. The PIC serviced the cooler and noticed a large buildup on the filters. The filters were cleaned but before the inspector left the internal thermometer was observed still at 60F. The cooler may require time for the temperature to come down after cleaning the filters; however, they cannot store any TCS foods inside the cooler until it is below 41F. They should schedule maintenance if the cooler temperature does not drop below 41F. The inspector will follow-up on 6/24/2025 to check on the temperature of the cooler.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine had a concentration of 0 ppm (Cl). The chemical sanitizers for dish machines must have a minimum concentration of 100 ppm. The heat of the dish machine was 111F. The dish machine was tested at the end of the entire cycle and at the end of the rinse cycle. It appears that the dish machine was testing low due to an air bubble in the line. After being properly primed, the dish machine was testing at 100ppm. Owner was initally notified of the concern and could not produce someone knowledgeable about properly using and testing the machine. 
After leaving the facility, the owner called to state the machine was operating properly. CK returned with HM to observe the machine primed at that time with an MJ Kellner representative to service the machine and a chemical log created to monitor the concentration of the machine at least three times per day. Discussed educating staff on service and testing. MJ Kellner representative confirmed he would educate available staff on methods to problem solve.

Ensure that chemical sanitizers meet the proper criteria and are tested regularly.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).
